thread:
sara (acme): Hey, ran into a blocker after upgrading to your Go client v2.0.1. Build fails with a module path error.

sam (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact error and your go.mod?

sara (acme): Sure. Error when running `go build`: 
```
go: github.com/redwood/go-client@v2.0.1: parsing go.mod:
	module declares its path as: github.com/redwood/go-client
	but was required as: github.com/redwood/go-client/v2
```
My go.mod: 
```
module acme/service

require (
    github.com/redwood/go-client/v2 v2.0.1
)
replace github.com/redwood/go-client/v2 => ../local/redwood-go
```
I also tried `go get github.com/redwood/go-client/v2@v2.0.1` and got the same parse error.

elaine (eng): That root error usually means the published v2 tag's go.mod has the wrong module path (missing the /v2 suffix). Can you `cat` the go.mod inside your module cache for that version? (or paste the output of `go env GOPATH` + ls of pkg/mod)

sara (acme): I can't easily inspect the cache on CI, but I checked the vendor copy from the release tarball. The module line in the packaged go.mod is `module github.com/redwood/go-client` (no /v2).

sam (support): Ok that matches the symptom — the v2 tag was published but the go.mod file wasn't updated to `module github.com/redwood/go-client/v2`. Eng team, is that a publish script issue?

jason (eng): Looks like the release tooling forgot to run the v2 module path bump step for the v2.0.1 tag. Should be fixed in the repo but that tag is already out. Two options: push a patched v2.0.2 with corrected go.mod, or advise users to use the non-v2 import path (not recommended).

elaine (eng): For immediate mitigation, remove the replace and point to the corrected tag once we publish. Workaround for CI: add this to your go.mod in the app (not ideal):
```
replace github.com/redwood/go-client/v2 => github.com/redwood/go-client v2.0.1
```
But that only helps if the module proxy accepts the tarball; the root issue persists. We'll cut a new release ASAP.

sam (support): Sara, can you try this local workaround to unblock CI? In your project's go.mod add the replace line above, run `go clean -modcache && go mod tidy` and re-run build. If you can share CI logs we can verify.

sara (acme): Will try and report back. One more Q: our code imports `github.com/redwood/go-client/v2` everywhere. Is that the expected public path for v2?

ajson (eng): Yes — public v2 modules must be imported with the /v2 suffix and the module declaration inside the v2 tag's go.mod must also include /v2. Publishing without that leads to the parse error you're seeing.

ci-bot: CI pipeline failed: go build (exit code 1) — see job #4521 logs: https://ci.example.com/acme/4521

elaine (eng): We're cutting v2.0.2 that fixes the go.mod module path and re-tagging. ETA about 30 minutes. We'll post here when done.

sam (support): Thanks — once v2.0.2 is out, please run `go get github.com/redwood/go-client/v2@v2.0.2` and remove any local replace hacks. If you still hit errors, paste the `go env` and full `go list -m -json github.com/redwood/go-client/v2@v2.0.2` output.

sara (acme): Thanks, trying workaround now. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:

(30m later) elaine (eng): v2.0.2 published and verified. The go.mod in the v2.0.2 tag declares `module github.com/redwood/go-client/v2`. We also triggered a proxy reindex.

sam (support): Sara, can you confirm CI passes now?

sara (acme): CI green! `go build` and `go test` both succeed after switching to v2.0.2 and removing the replace. Thanks everyone. :tada:

elaine (eng): Follow-up: internal note for release process — add an automated check that vN tags include matching module path suffix in go.mod before pushing tag. Filed ticket RLW-1423.

sam (support): Closing this thread once we confirm no other customers affected. Logged customer incident ID: INC-2026-334.

sara (acme): All good from our side. Cheers! :rocket
